changelog.change: Initial entry — method efficacy table with key counselling points, plus emergency contraception options and timing.

summary: LARC methods (implant, IUDs) are the most effective and are MEC category 1 for most conditions. The copper IUD is the most effective emergency contraception if placed within 5 days. Ulipristal outperforms levonorgestrel in the 72–120 h window; both lose efficacy at higher body weight.

rows: 3 years; subdermal progestin rod; amenorrhoea common; MEC 1 for most conditions
5–8 years; reduces bleeding; also treats heavy menstrual bleeding; can insert any time in the cycle
10–12 years; non-hormonal; the most effective EC if placed ≤ 5 days after unprotected sex
150 mg IM q12 weeks; reversible ↓ BMD with prolonged use; delayed return of fertility (9–18 months)
Daily; VTE risk from oestrogen; MEC 3–4 in smokers ≥ 35 y; 24/4 or 21/7 formulations
Safe with breastfeeding, hypertension, smoking, migraine with aura; strict timing (norethindrone ± 3 h)
The only method giving STI protection; pair with a hormonal method for dual efficacy
Most effective EC; also gives ongoing contraception
1.5 mg PO as soon as possible; best ≤ 72 h, works up to 120 h
Reduced efficacy at higher body weight (≳ 70–75 kg / BMI ≥ 26); OTC
Better than levonorgestrel in the 72–120 h window; also less weight-limited; prescription required

body.text: Quick-start any method the same day if pregnancy can be reasonably excluded; use a backup method for 7 days (2 days for the progestin-only pill). After ulipristal, delay starting a hormonal method for 5 days (it competes at the progesterone receptor).
